deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a verbatim excerpt that Riemann copied from Herbart. The header reads 'Herbart W. I. p. 507', presumably Herbart's Werke, Hartenstein's edition, vol. I, p. 507. The exact work within that volume is not identified here.

Content of the passage, paraphrased: Wherever anything spatial or temporal is thought, poeticized, dreamt, seen or felt, or used as a symbol to illustrate non-spatial objects, the represented content must spread apart in an ordered way 'drinnen' (inside, i.e. within the representing mind). This is because representing contains an ordered striving (Streben). By this striving each smallest partial representation (Partialvorstellung) draws all the others after it in a definite order of succession and weaves them into itself.

The task, Herbart says, was to explain how this striving and acting gets into the representations. To posit instead an infinitely empty vessel, into which the senses pour their sensations with no ground for arrangement or shape, was a contentless hypothesis that makes nothing comprehensible. This is an implicit polemic against Kant's view of space as an a priori form of intuition.

Riemann underlined 'drinnen' and the clause 'Zu erklären, wie dieses Streben und Wirken in die Vorstellungen komme'. This shows his interest in an internal, constructive origin of spatial order: space as generated by ordered series of representations (Herbart's 'Reihenformen'), not as a given receptacle.

The passage serves no computational problem. It is philosophical background to Riemann's notion of a manifold (Mannigfaltigkeit) as a continuous ordered system of determinations (Bestimmungsweisen), and to his natural-philosophical fragments. The previous folio is an excerpt of a review of Allihn's survey of Herbart's school, which confirms that this part of the bundle consists of Herbart reading notes.

results.what: Excerpt of Herbart's psychological account of space: spatial order arises from ordered series of partial representations, against Kant's 'empty vessel' conception of space
results.modern_name: Herbart's theory of 'Reihenformen' (serial forms) as the psychological origin of spatial and temporal order; background to Riemann's concept of a manifold
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25, and related writings); Herbart's influence on Riemann was analyzed by E. Scholz (Historia Mathematica 1982) and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copied quotation from Herbart with no mathematical content. Riemann's self-description as a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology, and Herbart's influence on his manifold concept, are well documented. The page only confirms the reading behind that known influence.

The phrase 'Zu erklären, wie dieses Streben und Wirken in die Vorstellungen komme' is underlined in the manuscript.

'hineinverflicht' is plausible from the image (Herbart's wording may be 'hineinverflicht' or 'verflicht'). The '[?]' can probably be dropped, but this should be checked against the printed Herbart text.
